"Supplerende indikator: Hjertesvigt efter atrieflimren" (Supplementary indicator: Heart failure after atrial fibrillation) is a clinical metric used within the Danish healthcare system to identify the development of heart failure as a complication following a new diagnosis of atrial fibrillation [^src1]. Its primary significance lies in supporting the assessment of long-term treatment effects and the overall quality of care provided to these patients [^src1].

The indicator is documented as part of the [[atrieflimren-i-danmark|Atrieflimren i Danmark]] report, an initiative by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) that monitors clinical quality indicators for atrial fibrillation treatment and management [^src1]. In the report's analysis, this supplementary metric is evaluated alongside primary indicators, such as severe bleeding within one year of a new diagnosis (Indicator 11) and heart failure within one year of a new diagnosis (Indicator 15) [^src1]. 

To facilitate quality improvement and policy governance, the data for this indicator is presented not only at the national level but also broken down by regions, health clusters, and specific cluster areas [^src1]. This detailed stratification allows healthcare administrators and clinicians to compare regional performance, identify variations in clinical practices, and evaluate differences in patient outcomes across Denmark [^src1].
